items.title: OMH (Oh My Hermes) is a workflow skill pack for Hermes Agent, bringing reusable methods for developm...
items.content:
OMH (Oh My Hermes) is a workflow skill pack for Hermes Agent, bringing reusable methods for development, research, and business analysis.

https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E

Its omh-market-research skill helps investigate a market before committing to a product, customer segment, or pricing decision.

For example, imagine you’re considering an AI customer-support tool for small e-commerce teams in South Korea.

You could ask:

“Use omh-market-research to assess this opportunity before we build. Examine the addressable market, comparable alternatives, and customer evidence. Show the assumptions, evidence gaps, and what could change the decision.”

The workflow structures that investigation:

• Market sizing: Estimate demand from eligible buyers and annual spending. Separate the total market from the segment you can serve and the customers your team can realistically reach—not an arbitrary percentage of a large industry.

• Competitive pricing: Compare alternatives under the same workload. Include minimum seats, usage allowances, overages, and annual commitments before comparing per-seat subscriptions with per-resolution fees.

• Customer evidence: Examine current workarounds, purchase triggers, switching costs, and past behavior. Keep stated interest separate from observed commitments. Reviews are evidence to examine, not proof that customers will pay.

• Sensitivity: Test how lower spending, conversion, or reachable demand changes the opportunity. Identify which missing evidence could reverse the decision.

The intended output is an inspectable brief with sources, calculations, assumptions, competing evidence, and next validation steps.

A capable model can do this with the right instructions. OMH packages the method into a reusable workflow, so you don’t have to reconstruct the research process for every new idea.
